title: An Idea Becomes a Connected System — Ukiyo-e dawn print on cool rice-white paper (preview)

scenes.title: The wave carries the idea to the fleet
scenes.purpose: A persimmon dawn sun (the idea) rises over an indigo sea printed on cool rice-white paper. Persimmon tow-cords join three boats into one fleet. A cropped wave rears up and its swell lifts each linked boat in turn, so the idea becomes a connected system.
visuals: Fixed cool rice-white paper #E4E8E2 with seeded Canvas 2D indigo/key fibre, reused as a multiply layer over the plates
Stepped bokashi sky from indigo through blue to paper, with a restrained stepped paper-to-persimmon akabokashi band at the horizon
Patterned cloud bands with key contour and an ochre kasumi stripe
Distant mountain with an inset indigo plate and a paper snowcap over the key block
Asymmetric wave cropped at the left edge: key fill, inset indigo plate, blue face plate and fine key contour
Refined foam claws along the crest and frozen spray droplets in paper colour
Persimmon sun disc with a persimmon reflection on the water
Three ochre boats with rowers, joined by persimmon tow-cords
Static title cartouche on the right reading 'An Idea Becomes a Connected System' on a paper backing
Caption strip reading 'ORIGINAL STUDY · EDO WAVE-PRINT IDIOM'

beats.development: The persimmon sun pops in (0.1-0.6s) and its reflection plate spreads across the water. The wave swells from a low crest to a rising crest (morph A→B, 0.2-1.0s). Tow-cords draw boat to boat (0.55-1.4s). Petals start drifting in from the left, and the cloud band pans slowly.

The crest curls into a cropped claw (morph B→C, 1.0-1.75s). Its swell lifts the linked boats one after another (0.95s, 1.2s and 1.45s starts), and the cords flex with them. Foam claws bloom along the crest (1.7-2.55s).
Spray thrown from the crest comes to rest as frozen spray. The petals and cloud band settle by 2.6s, and the complete print holds for reading until 3.0s.

findings: All motion finishes by 2.6s, so the composition is settled before 2.7s.
The wave morph changes a large share of the left of the frame, well above the 8% pixel-change threshold, and the paper stays fixed.
Text sits on its own paper backing: #283C49 on #E4E8E2 is about 9.2:1 and #385F84 on #E4E8E2 about 5.4:1. Persimmon is used only for non-text shapes.
justifiedHolds: The 2.6-3.0s hold lets the viewer read the title cartouche and the finished print.

notes: This is an original study in the Edo wave-print idiom and does not claim to copy a specific historical print.
All state comes from the paused GSAP timeline time and is redrawn on hf-seek.
Typography uses a declared @font-face 'Print Mincho' that resolves to local Mincho/serif faces (local() sources only), falling back to Georgia/serif.
print-scene.js builds the static plates and exposes the time-derived render(t). index.html builds the paused GSAP timeline inline and registers it at window.__timelines.video.

Source-frame refresh: BACKGROUND_REVIEW.json (ambiguous-ai-389509, contact sheet second 7) shows a print idiom of flat indigo waves and a vermilion sun disc on paper. Following its background suggestion, the warm #F0E6C9 paper is replaced by a cool rice-white paper with indigo and persimmon print colours for a dawn scene. Its subject, glyph, die, cartouche lettering and layout are not copied.

No reviewed preview recipes were supplied (the optional recipe list is empty and STYLE.json has no tech.preview_recipes), so this preview demonstrates the primary implementation with the scene-dependent palette refresh.
